children: Agentic AI could threaten a broad group of consumer-facing companies whose businesses depend on people visiting their websites and apps, according to JPMorgan.
The bank argues that increasingly capable AI agents could weaken business models built around search friction, consumer inertia, switching costs and control over online traffic.
The risk is straightforward.

If consumers begin asking AI agents to search for products, compare prices, book trips or shop for financial services on their behalf, they may have less reason to visit traditional websites and apps directly.
That could mean fewer visits, leads and transactions for companies whose economics depend on owning the customer interface.
JPMorgan's U.S. Consumer Agentic AI Vulnerable basket spans travel, marketplaces, fintech, insurance, advertising and online discovery.
The five largest positions in the basket are:
Ally Financial
carries a 7.1% weight and is down 14% year to date.
Rocket Companies
represents 7.0% of the basket and has fallen 38% this year.
Booking Holdings
has a 6.8% weight and is down 27%.
Expedia
also represents 6.8% and has declined 8%.
Airbnb
rounds out the top five at 6.8%, although its stock is up 12% year to date.

here
Investor takeaway
JPMorgan's concern is less about AI replacing these companies outright and more about AI potentially sitting between them and their customers.

That could be especially disruptive for businesses built around discovery, comparison or lead generation because an AI agent may increasingly perform those functions before a consumer ever reaches the platform.
For investors, the key question is whether these companies can make themselves indispensable to AI agents rather than simply becoming traffic sources that agents bypass.

The metrics to watch will be direct traffic, customer-acquisition costs, conversion rates, lead volumes and whether these companies can integrate their own agentic tools quickly enough to defend the customer relationship.

title: JPMorgan Names Stocks Most Exposed to Agentic AI
